title: Unlocking Data Control: The Key to Modern Property Management
excerpt: Discover why owning your data and digital infrastructure is crucial for commercial real estate. Learn how to empower your property management with actionable insights.
content:
In today's rapidly evolving commercial real estate (CRE) landscape, owning your data and digital infrastructure isn't just an advantage—it's a necessity. This insight was at the heart of the inaugural episode of the Peak Property Performance® Podcast, where OpticWise leaders Bill Douglas and Drew Hall shared their expert perspectives on how data control can transform property management and ownership.

Understanding the Vision Behind the Podcast

Bill Douglas and Drew Hall launched the Peak Property Performance Podcast to address a critical gap in the CRE industry: the lack of actionable business intelligence. During the episode, Bill explained that many property owners express a desire for data-driven decision-making but lack the necessary data control to achieve it. He emphasized, "If you don't own your data & digital infrastructure, your vendors do." This podcast aims to empower property owners and operators with the knowledge they need to reclaim control over their digital assets.

As co-host Drew Hall noted, the podcast is not about the buzzword-heavy "PropTech" solutions but the foundational digital infrastructure that supports them. The goal is to demystify the complexities of digital infrastructure and AI, making them accessible to all property owners, regardless of their technical background.

The Role of Business Intelligence in CRE

Business intelligence is a game-changer in CRE, but without the right data, it's just a buzzword. Drew highlighted the transformative power of harnessing data, explaining how seemingly minor adjustments can lead to significant financial improvements. "It's impressive, the differences that can be made by sometimes just making one little mod over here or capturing something that you didn't even realize you weren't capturing," he noted.

This approach aligns with the OpticWise PPP 5C™ framework—Clarify, Connect, Collect, Coordinate, Control—which guides property owners in effectively managing their digital infrastructure to maximize data utility.

Clarifying the Non-PropTech Focus

Bill and Drew were clear about the podcast's departure from traditional PropTech discussions. Instead of focusing on software solutions, they are diving deeper into the underlying digital infrastructure that supports these technologies. Bill explained, "PropTech has to run on a digital infrastructure, may or may not generate data, but it's going to use data." The emphasis is on owning and controlling this infrastructure, which is the real driver of property performance.

The OpticWise 5S® UX standard—Seamless Mobility, Security, Stability, Speed, Service—plays a crucial role in enhancing user experiences across properties, further underscoring the importance of robust digital foundations.

Key Challenges in Commercial Real Estate

In their client interactions, Bill and Drew often encounter three main challenges: occupancy, insurance, and utilities. By controlling the technology user experience, property owners can increase occupancy rates, attract tech-savvy tenants, and reduce insurance premiums and utility costs.

Bill shared a powerful example: "We typically see expense, like insurance premiums, instead of 10 to 12% like a year, we've seen them go down to just one or two with the right amount of data to the underwriter." These improvements directly impact Net Operating Income (NOI), demonstrating the tangible benefits of data ownership.

Data Ownership and Digital Infrastructure

The central theme of the episode was clear: who owns and controls your data flow and digital infrastructure? Without ownership, property owners are at the mercy of their vendors. Bill challenged listeners to imagine the possibilities of full data control, stating, "Imagine what you could do if you were able to look across disparate data sources within your property and within your portfolio to draw conclusions and actually make actionable decisions that are data-driven."

This forward-thinking approach is crucial for CRE owners who want to remain competitive and future-proof their assets.

Encouragement to Explore and Innovate

Both hosts emphasized the importance of not shying away from the complexities of digital infrastructure. Drew encouraged listeners by saying, "Don't be afraid to dig in. There's a lot there. But like I said in the first answer, there is a lot of benefit to digging in." By exploring and understanding their digital assets, property owners can uncover hidden opportunities for growth and efficiency.

For a deeper dive into these strategies and concepts, listeners can explore the Peak Property Performance book, which provides a comprehensive guide to implementing these practices.

Actionable Takeaway for CRE Owners

The inaugural episode of the Peak Property Performance Podcast serves as a wake-up call for CRE owners to take control of their data and digital infrastructure. By doing so, they can unlock powerful business intelligence, optimize operations, and enhance tenant experiences. The journey to Peak Property Performance begins with a single question: who owns your data?
